evidence.quote: let statement (customerId: string) (currency: string) (from: DateOnly) (until: DateOnly) (r: Receivables) : Result<Statement, string> =
match Statements.statement customerId "USD" from until books, books.Books.Customers.TryFind customerId with

ARC-REV-01.rationale: All statement rules are in the Tier 1/2 Summa.Ledger.Statements module. These rules cover which invoices count, how settlement entries map to line kinds, the clamp to the issue date, the ordering, the opening balance and the running balance. They reuse Payments.settlement. The Tier 2 engine handler only resolves the range, calls the Ledger function and offers the result. The Tier 3 wire adds only an event-to-Msg mapping (AccountingWire.fs:122). The export permission check goes through the existing updateBooks gate (Accounting.fs:242).

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is introduced below Tier 4. Statements.fs is pure. It uses only DateOnly formatting and a StringBuilder, and no System.IO, System.Net, System.Text.Json or clock. The engine handler uses the model's `Today` (supplied with each message) and requests the file as data with `OfferDownload`, which is the existing engine-effect path that the host performs. No clock, random or GUID is read.

evidence.quote: /// A JSON string as the invoice document's writer writes it: ASCII only, ... let private quoted (text: string) =

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The JSON string-escaping rules are copied from the invoice document writer instead of referencing it. The classification text is restated as a new literal although it is described as what every financial export says. The "USD" currency is hard-coded in the engine handler. The copies agree with the existing definitions, but they can drift. Other facts have a single definition: settlement from Payments.settlement and the date ranges from Accounting.dateRange.

evidence.quote: invoices |> List.filter (fun i -> bucket until i.DueDate = b) |> List.map part |> sum currency

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The aging split lives in the Tier 1/2 Ledger statement function and reuses Payments.bucket for the due-date rule. The CSV layout lives in Ledger as well. The engine handler only wires the request to the Exports.withHeader and Ledger functions, and the Tier 3 wire adds only an event mapping. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 site re-derives a rule.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect enters Tier 1/2. toCsv and the aging code are pure. The engine takes the generation time from `ctx.Now`, as the follow-up's header requires, and returns the file through the existing `OfferDownload` effect-as-data path. The data version comes from the existing pure Exports.dataVersion. Nothing reads the clock or does I/O below Tier 4.

evidence.quote: String.Join(",", [ isoDate date; kind; Reports.csvField invoice; Reports.csvField reference; amount; balance ])

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The follow-up adds no restated fact. It makes the existing Reports.decimalText public and reuses it, together with Reports.csvField, Exports.withHeader, Payments.bucket and the existing kindText and isoDate, instead of copying them. The JSON and CSV outputs share the same Statement value. The version literal is bumped in one place (JsonVersion = 2). The JSON escaper and classification duplication from change set 1 is not touched or worsened.
